Legal Services Corporation
AGENCY:
Legal Services Corporation.
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
The Legal Services Corporation (LSC) announces revisions to Performance Area One of its Performance Criteria. In Performance Area One, LSC established the indicators that LSC will use to evaluate grant recipients' processes for identifying the most pressing and emerging legal needs in their service areas and determining how they will deliver legal services tailored to most effectively address those needs. LSC is adopting a new criterion assessing strategic planning in addition to revising the existing criteria examining grant recipients' conduct of needs assessments, implementation of strategies to address legal needs, and self-examination of their effectiveness in delivering legal services.
DATES:
The revised Performance Area will become effective on January 1, 2027.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Stefanie K. Davis, Deputy General Counsel, Legal Services Corporation, 1825 I Street NW, Suite 800, Washington, DC 20006, 202-295-1563,
performancearea1@lsc.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
LSC is revising Performance Area One of its Performance Criteria for the first time since 2007. The revisions to Performance Area One reflect trends in the delivery of legal services, particularly with respect to the evolution in non-profit management, including the increased use of technology; the increasing prevalence of state access to justice commissions; and a changed legal aid funding landscape. While the detail in and number of Areas of Inquiry and Indicators have expanded through this Revision, LSC's intention for the Performance Criteria has not changed. The Criteria remain, as LSC stated in 2007, “a useful framework for internal program self-evaluations, planning, and program development, as well as external peer reviews and expert assessments by other funding sources,
(
printed page 66168)
such as IOLTA programs and government agencies.” Legal Services Corporation, Performance Criteria, p. 1 (March 2007).
LSC undertook the Revisions to Performance Area One for several reasons. First, nonprofit management has evolved greatly in the last two decades focusing on increased professionalism, revenue diversification, data-driven accountability, and enhanced board governance and leadership practices.
Additionally, in 2021, the American Bar Association adopted revisions to its Standards for the Provision of Civil Legal Aid (Standards). The 2006 Standards guided LSC's development of the 2007 Performance Criteria. Consequently, LSC determined that it was appropriate to review and revise the Performance Criteria to the extent that they complement the Standards.
In a similar vein, LSC was motivated to update Performance Area One to reflect the efficiencies developed by legal services providers and created by technology. The delivery of legal services has changed significantly since 2007, with case management systems becoming more sophisticated in terms of the data they can collect and aggregate; legal aid organizations and courts conducting more business through videoconferencing and providing more legal information via mobile apps; and the nascence of artificial intelligence in intake and case management. Technological changes have also affected the ways in which legal services organizations and their partners conduct needs assessments and engage in strategic planning. The revisions to Performance Area One take these changes into account and ask evaluators to consider whether, and to what extent, legal aid organizations are using these strategies in their planning and operations.
Finally, LSC wanted to improve the structure and utility of Performance Area One as an evaluation tool. Although LSC has introduced new Areas of Inquiry and Indicators, LSC is presenting all Areas and Indicators in simpler, clearer language. LSC has also reorganized and renamed the four Criteria within Performance Area One to better reflect the needs assessment, strategic planning, implementation, and evaluation cycle.
LSC published the revisions to Performance Area One for public comment in early October 2025. During the comment period, LSC received eleven unique comments from executive directors of LSC grantees, collectives of LSC grantees, and national legal organizations. These commenters raised several concerns centered around the idea that LSC was taking the Performance Criteria in a more prescriptive direction. First, they stated that the proposed language appeared to turn the Performance Criteria into another enforcement tool rather than guidance. Second, they expressed concern that LSC was emphasizing numbers of clients served rather than overall impact on the client population in a grantee's service area. Finally, they opined that it appeared LSC expected all grantees, regardless of size, funding level, or service area characteristics, to conform to the same rigid schedule and elements of needs assessment and strategic planning. LSC did not intend to change the evaluation-centered focus of Performance Area One or to require all grantees to focus only on serving as many individual clients as possible, regardless of the needs in their respective service areas. LSC appreciates the concerns raised by these commenters and has revised the introduction to Performance Area One, introductions to each of the Criteria, and the Areas of Inquiry and Indicators as needed to resolve those concerns.
LSC has published the revised Performance Area 1 on its website at
https://www.lsc.gov/​our-impact/​publications/​other-publications-and-reports/​lsc-performance-criteria
.
LSC will begin using the revised Performance Area 1 on January 1, 2027. LSC recognizes that it may take time, guidance, and experience for all grantees to adjust to the revisions. LSC will, therefore, provide training and forums to discuss the implementation of the changes. When conducting program assessments, LSC staff will take the scope of the revisions and each program's capacity into consideration when making recommendations.
Overview of Changes
LSC revised Performance Area One to clarify and enhance existing guidance by presenting a more structured and integrated framework for legal aid organizations to consider in carrying out their work. The current version of the Performance Criteria describes core concepts in a more narrative format. The proposed revisions reorganize these concepts to more clearly reflect the relationship among needs assessment, strategic planning, priority setting, and evaluation. This reorganization is intended to help grantees understand how these activities may operate together as part of an ongoing process, while preserving flexibility and not prescribing a single required approach.
The proposed revisions also provide additional details to illustrate considerations that may inform an organization's approach. For example, under Criterion 1 (Needs Assessment), the proposed indicators describe a range of methods that organizations might use to identify the most pressing legal needs of their client communities, including consultation with community partners, review of available data, and use of information gathered during statewide assessments (see Proposed Indicators 1 and 2). The new indicators further describe ways in which organizations may consider the needs of different populations and the role that other service providers in the service area play in serving their shared client populations (see Proposed Indicators 3 and 4). These revisions are intended to provide greater clarity regarding the types of information that may be relevant to a comprehensive assessment, without requiring the use of any particular methodology.
Under Criterion 2 (Strategic Planning), the proposed revisions describe how organizations might use the results of a needs assessment to inform planning processes. For example, the proposed indicators ask questions about how the results of a grantee's needs assessment influence the grantee's development of a written strategic plan (see Proposed Indicator 1). Additional indicators describe considerations that may inform the planning process, such as stakeholder engagement, use of quantitative and qualitative data, and alignment with organizational capacity and resources (see Proposed Indicators 2 through 4). These provisions are intended to identify factors that grantees may consider when structuring their planning efforts.
The revisions to Criterion 3 (Priority Setting and Case Acceptance Policy) describe how organizations might translate planning decisions into operational practices. For example, the proposed indicators address the establishment of service priorities that reflect identified needs and strategic objectives, as well as the adoption of a written case acceptance policy to guide service delivery (see Proposed Indicators 1 and 3). The new indicators also describe alternative approaches that organizations may consider when full representation is not feasible, including referrals, collaboration with other providers, and the use of technology (see Proposed Indicator 4). These examples are intended to help organizations consider a range of options for delivering services within available resources.
Finally, under Criterion 4 (Evaluation), the revised indicators
(
printed page 66169)
describe approaches that grantees might use to assess the effectiveness of their work and make appropriate adjustments over time. These include evaluating the alignment of services with established priorities, using data and stakeholder input to inform decision-making, and maintaining flexibility to respond to changing conditions (see Proposed Indicators 1 and 2). The revisions also describe the role of ongoing review in supporting continuous improvement and responsiveness to emerging needs.
Overall, LSC intended the revisions to improve the clarity, organization, and usability of the Performance Criteria by providing more detailed lists of factors that grantees may find useful. LSC did not intend to establish new requirements, but rather to offer guidance that legal aid organizations may adapt based on their individual circumstances, including their size, capacity, and the needs of the communities they serve.

Forest Service
AGENCY:
Forest Service, Agriculture (USDA).
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
The Eldorado National Forest is proposing to establish several recreation fee sites and a special recreation permit. Proposed recreation fees collected at the proposed recreation fee sites and for the proposed special recreation permit would be used for operation, maintenance, and improvement of the sites and the special recreation use covered by the proposed special recreation permit. An analysis of nearby recreation fee sites and special recreation uses with similar amenities shows that the proposed recreation fees are reasonable and typical of similar recreation fee sites and special recreation uses in the area.
DATES:
If approved, the proposed recreation fee sites and proposed recreation fees would be established no earlier than six months following the publication of this notice in the
Federal Register
.
ADDRESSES:
Eldorado National Forest, Attention: Recreation Fees, 100 Forni Road, Placerville, CA 95667.
(
printed page 66075)
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Don Morrill, Forest Recreation Officer, (530) 957-0740,
don.morrill@usda.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The Federal Lands Recreation Enhancement Act (
16 U.S.C. 6803(b)
) requires the Forest Service to publish in the
Federal Register
a six-month advance notice before the establishment of a new recreation fee area. In accordance with Forest Service Handbook 2309.13, chapter 30, the Forest Service will publish the proposed recreation fee sites, proposed recreation fees, and proposed special recreation permit in local newspapers and other local publications for public comment. At least 80 percent of the proposed recreation fees collected at the Eldorado National Forest would remain available for expenditure at the Forest to enhance the visitor experience at the proposed recreation fee sites and in connection with the special recreation use covered by the proposed special recreation permit.
A proposed expanded amenity recreation fee of $26 per night would be charged for Airport Flat Campground, Azalea Cove Campground, Camino Cove Campground, Cole Creek Camping Area, and Lone Rock Campground. A proposed expanded amenity recreation fee of $46 per night would be charged for double sites at Camino Cove Campground. In addition, a proposed expanded amenity recreation fee of $100 per night would be charged for rental of Bunker Hill Lookout Cabin.
A proposed standard amenity recreation fee of $10 per day per vehicle would be charged at Echo Summit Nordic Ski Area, Fleming Meadow, Caples Creek, Lake Margaret, Shealor Lake, and Thunder Mountain trailheads and developed recreation sites. The America the Beautiful—the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Pass would be honored at these standard amenity recreation fee sites. A special recreation permit and a fee of $10 per person, per night, are proposed for overnight camping in the Mokelumne Carson Pass Management Area during the first year of implementation. During years 2 through 4, the fee would remain at $10 per person, per night, with an increase to $15 per person, per night beginning in year 5.
Fee revenue would be used to enhance recreation opportunities, improve customer service, and address maintenance needs.
Once public involvement is complete, the proposed recreation fee sites, proposed special recreation permits, and proposed recreation fees will be reviewed by a Resource Advisory Committee prior to a final decision and implementation. Reservations for campgrounds and cabins can be made online at
www.recreation.gov
or by calling (877) 444-6777. A Reservation fee of $8.00 per reservation will be added to the cost of the reservation. The $8.00 reservation fee is a transaction fee charged by the
recreation.gov
reservation platform and is not a Forest Service recreation fee under the Federal Lands Recreation Enhancement Act. This transaction fee is retained by the service provider to support the cost of the reservation system.
Gordon Blum,
Associate Deputy Chief, Recreation and Heritage.

0.20
Currently, this tiered schedule of rebates is followed by five examples (labeled Example 1 through Example 5) that illustrate how the program works. Finally, rebates under this program are currently capped at $2,000,000 per member or member organization in a given month.
First Change
The Exchange proposes to increase the Tier 1 Per Contract Rebate (when there is a Customer on one side) from $0.04 to $0.07. This change will bring this Tier 1 rebate to the same level as the Tier 2 rebate.
Second Change
The Exchange proposes to increase the Tier 1 Per Contract Rebate (when there are Non-Customers on both sides) from $0.10 to $0.18. This change will bring this Tier 1 rebate to the same level as the Tier 2 rebate.
[
10
]
Third Change
The Exchange proposes to make several changes to Examples 2,
[
11
]
3, and 4 to reflect the new rebate levels.
Fourth Change
The Exchange proposes to make a change to Example 4 to correct an oversight from a prior filing,
[
12
]
that had decreased the Tier 4 rebate (when there are Non-Customers on both sides) from $0.22 to $0.20, but had not adjusted its corresponding example. This is not a substantive change.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
13
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
14
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
15
]
Likewise, in
NetCoalition
v.
Securities and Exchange Commission
[
16
]
(“NetCoalition”) the D.C. Circuit upheld the Commission's use of a market-based approach in evaluating the fairness of market data fees against a challenge claiming that Congress mandated a cost-based approach.
[
17
]
As the court emphasized, the Commission “intended in Regulation NMS that `market forces, rather than regulatory requirements' play a role in determining the market data . . . to be made available to investors and at what cost.”
[
18
]
Further, “[n]o one disputes that competition for order flow is `fierce.' . . . As the SEC explained, `[i]n the U.S. national market system, buyers and sellers of securities, and the broker-dealers that act as their order-routing agents, have a wide range of choices of where to route orders for execution'; [and] `no exchange can afford to take its market share percentages for granted' because `no exchange possesses a monopoly, regulatory or otherwise, in the execution of order flow from broker dealers'. . . .”
[
19
]
Although the court and the SEC were discussing the cash equities markets, the Exchange believes
(
printed page 66189)
that these views apply with equal force to the options markets.
First Change
The Exchange believes that its proposal to increase the Tier 1 Per Contract Rebate for qualifying volume with a Customer on one side from $0.04 to $0.07 is reasonable. As discussed above, this change is designed to increase the amount of the rebate available to Floor Brokers at the entry-level tier of the Floor Broker Incentive Program, thereby providing a stronger incentive for Floor Brokers to direct qualifying open outcry order flow with a Customer on one side to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed increase will make the Floor Broker Incentive Program more attractive at the entry level and will encourage additional Floor Brokers to participate in the Program. Increased participation in the Program will bring additional Customer order flow to the Exchange, which benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities and deeper liquidity, particularly for open outcry executions on the Exchange's Trading Floor. The proposed Tier 1 rebate of $0.07 per contract is reasonable because it is the same per contract rebate that the Exchange currently pays for qualifying volume with a Customer on one side at the Tier 2 volume level. The proposed change is therefore consistent with the rebate levels that the Exchange has previously determined to be reasonable under this same Program.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed increase in the Tier 1 Per Contract Rebate for qualifying volume with a Customer on one side is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the proposed rebate will apply uniformly to all Floor Brokers that satisfy the Tier 1 volume threshold under the Floor Broker Incentive Program. Any Floor Broker is able to qualify for the Tier 1 rebate by satisfying the objective, transparent volume threshold of up to 500,000 qualifying contracts, and all qualifying Floor Brokers will receive the same $0.07 per contract rebate on qualifying volume with a Customer on one side within that threshold. The Exchange believes it is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory to offer this rebate in respect of qualifying volume with a Customer on one side because Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts Market Makers. An increase in the activity of these market participants in turn facilitates tighter spreads, which may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants.
Second Change
The Exchange believes that its proposal to increase the Tier 1 Per Contract Rebate for qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides from $0.10 to $0.18 is reasonable. As discussed above, this change is designed to increase the amount of the rebate available to Floor Brokers at the entry-level tier of the Floor Broker Incentive Program in respect of open outcry executions with Non-Customers on both sides, thereby providing a stronger incentive for Floor Brokers to direct such qualifying volume to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed increase will make the Program more attractive at the entry level and will encourage additional Floor Brokers to participate in the Program. Increased participation in the Program will bring additional order flow to the Exchange, which benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities and deeper liquidity, particularly for open outcry executions on the Exchange's Trading Floor. The proposed Tier 1 rebate of $0.18 per contract is reasonable because it is the same per contract rebate that the Exchange currently pays for qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides at the Tier 2 volume level (and, indeed, at the Tier 3 volume level). The proposed change is therefore consistent with the rebate levels that the Exchange has previously determined to be reasonable under this same Program.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed increase in the Tier 1 Per Contract Rebate for qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the proposed rebate will apply uniformly to all Floor Brokers that satisfy the Tier 1 volume threshold under the Floor Broker Incentive Program. Any Floor Broker is able to qualify for the Tier 1 rebate by satisfying the objective, transparent volume threshold of up to 500,000 qualifying contracts, and all qualifying Floor Brokers will receive the same $0.18 per contract rebate on qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides within that threshold. The Exchange believes it is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory to offer this rebate in respect of qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides because such open outcry activity supports the price discovery and liquidity provision functions of the Exchange's Trading Floor, which benefits all market participants.
Third Change
The Exchange believes that its proposal to make conforming changes to Examples 2, 3, and 4 to reflect the new Tier 1 rebate levels is consistent with the Act. This change is non-substantive and is designed to ensure that the illustrative examples that accompany the tiered rebate schedule accurately reflect the operation of the Floor Broker Incentive Program under the increased Tier 1 rebates proposed in the First and Second Changes. The Exchange believes that making these conforming changes to the examples will make the Pricing Schedule easier to read and will remove any potential confusion that could arise from having the examples reflect outdated rebate amounts. This change protects investors and the public interest by ensuring that the illustrative examples in the Pricing Schedule are accurate and consistent with the tiered rebate schedule as modified by this filing.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed changes to Examples 2, 3, and 4 are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because they are non-substantive and do not alter the fees or rebates available to any Floor Broker or category of Floor Brokers. The updated examples will apply uniformly to all Floor Brokers and will continue to illustrate the operation of the Program in the same manner for all similarly situated market participants.
Fourth Change
The Exchange believes that its proposal to correct Example 4 to reflect the currently applicable Tier 4 Per Contract Rebate of $0.20 per contract for qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides is consistent with the Act. As discussed above, this change is non-substantive and is designed to correct an oversight from a prior filing that had decreased the Tier 4 rebate (when there are Non-Customers on both sides) but had not simultaneously adjusted the corresponding figures in Example 4. The Exchange believes that correcting the example will make the Pricing Schedule easier to read and will eliminate any potential confusion that could arise from having the example reflect a rebate amount that is no longer in effect. This change protects investors and the public interest by ensuring that the illustrative examples in the Pricing Schedule are accurate and consistent with the tiered rebate schedule that is currently in effect.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed correction to Example 4 is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it is non-
(
printed page 66190)
substantive and does not alter the fees or rebates available to any Floor Broker or category of Floor Brokers. The corrected example will apply uniformly to all Floor Brokers and will continue to illustrate the operation of the Program in the same manner for all similarly situated market participants.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
Inter-Market Competition
The proposal does not impose an undue burden on inter-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange believes its proposal remains competitive with other options markets and will offer market participants another choice of where to transact options. The Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily favor competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive, or rebate opportunities available at other venues to be more favorable. In such an environment, the Exchange must continually adjust its fees to remain competitive with other exchanges. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees in response, and because market participants may readily adjust their order routing practices, the Exchange believes that the degree to which fee changes in this market may impose any burden on competition is extremely limited.
Intra-Market Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change would impose any burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
First Change
The Exchange does not believe that its proposal to increase the Tier 1 Per Contract Rebate for qualifying volume with a Customer on one side from $0.04 to $0.07 will impose any undue burden on intra-market competition. The proposed increased rebate will apply uniformly to all similarly situated market participants: any Floor Broker that satisfies the Tier 1 volume threshold under the Floor Broker Incentive Program will receive the same $0.07 per contract rebate on qualifying volume with a Customer on one side within that threshold. Any Floor Broker is able to qualify for the Tier 1 rebate by satisfying the objective, transparent volume threshold. The Exchange further believes that providing this rebate for qualifying volume with a Customer on one side does not impose an undue burden on intra-market competition because Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts Market Makers. An increase in the activity of these market participants in turn facilitates tighter spreads, which may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants. The proposed change is designed to enhance, rather than restrict, competition among Floor Brokers for open outcry Customer order flow by increasing the amount of the entry-level rebate available under the Program. To the extent Floor Brokers regard the proposed Tier 1 rebate as insufficient, they may readily direct their order flow to any of the other options exchanges that support open outcry executions.
Second Change
The Exchange does not believe that its proposal to increase the Tier 1 Per Contract Rebate for qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides from $0.10 to $0.18 will impose any undue burden on intra-market competition. The proposed increased rebate will apply uniformly to all similarly situated market participants: any Floor Broker that satisfies the Tier 1 volume threshold under the Floor Broker Incentive Program will receive the same $0.18 per contract rebate on qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides within that threshold. Any Floor Broker is able to qualify for the Tier 1 rebate by satisfying the objective, transparent volume threshold. The Exchange further believes that providing this rebate for qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides does not impose an undue burden on intra-market competition because open outcry activity on the Exchange's Trading Floor supports the price discovery and liquidity provision functions of the Trading Floor, which benefits all market participants. The proposed change is designed to enhance, rather than restrict, competition among Floor Brokers for open outcry order flow with Non-Customers on both sides by increasing the amount of the entry-level rebate available under the Program. To the extent Floor Brokers regard the proposed Tier 1 rebate as insufficient, they may readily direct their order flow to any of the other options exchanges that support open outcry executions.
Third Change
The Exchange does not believe that its proposal to make conforming changes to Examples 2, 3, and 4 will impose any burden on competition. As discussed above, this change is non-substantive and is intended to conform the illustrative examples in the Pricing Schedule to the increased Tier 1 rebates proposed in the First and Second Changes. Because the proposed change does not alter the fees or rebates available to any Floor Broker or category of Floor Brokers, and merely conforms the illustrative examples in the Pricing Schedule to the tiered rebate schedule as modified by this filing, it does not impose any burden on either intra-market or inter-market competition.
Fourth Change
The Exchange does not believe that its proposal to correct Example 4 will impose any burden on competition. As discussed above, this change is non-substantive and is intended to correct an oversight from a prior filing that had adjusted the Tier 4 Per Contract Rebate for qualifying volume with Non-Customers on both sides but had not simultaneously updated the corresponding figures in Example 4. Because the proposed change does not alter the fees or rebates available to any Floor Broker or category of Floor Brokers, and merely conforms the illustrative example to the tiered rebate schedule that is currently in effect, it does not impose any burden on either intra-market or inter-market competition.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
[
20
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is: (i) necessary or appropriate in the public interest; (ii) for the protection of investors; or (iii) otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings
(
printed page 66191)
to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-PHLX-2026-61 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-PHLX-2026-61. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-PHLX-2026-61 and should be submitted on or before November 9, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
21
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.

2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,

[

in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”

Likewise, in
NetCoalition

[

As the court emphasized, the Commission “intended in Regulation NMS that `market forces, rather than regulatory requirements' play a role in determining the market data . . . to be made available to investors and at what cost.”
[

Further, “[n]o one disputes that competition for order flow is `fierce.' . . . As the SEC explained, `[i]n the U.S. national market system, buyers and sellers of securities, and the broker-dealers that act as their order-routing agents, have a wide range of choices of where to route orders for execution'; [and] `no exchange can afford to take its market share percentages for granted' because `no exchange possesses a
(

monopoly, regulatory or otherwise, in the execution of order flow from broker dealers' . . . .”
[

]
Although the court and the SEC were discussing the cash equities markets, the Exchange believes that these views apply with equal force to the options markets.
The Exchange's proposed change to Options 7 is reasonable in several respects. As a threshold matter, the Exchange is subject to significant competitive forces in the market for options transaction services that constrain its pricing determinations in that market. Within this environment, the Exchange must continually adjust the fees and rebates set forth in its Pricing Schedule to remain competitive with the other national securities exchanges to which market participants may direct their options order flow.
The Exchange's proposal to reduce the rebate paid to NOM Market Makers to add liquidity in Penny Symbols by $0.01 per contract across each of the six existing tiers is reasonable because it represents a modest recalibration of the Exchange's Pricing Schedule that reflects the Exchange's ongoing efforts to balance the incentives it offers to NOM Market Makers against the costs and business considerations attendant to operating an options exchange in a highly competitive market. Even after the proposed reduction, NOM Market Makers will continue to receive meaningful rebates for adding liquidity in Penny Symbols, ranging from ($0.19) per contract at Tier 1 to ($0.44) per contract at Tier 6, and NOM Market Makers will retain the ability to increase the rebate they receive by adding greater volumes of qualifying liquidity in Penny Symbols on the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the amended rebates will remain competitive with rebates offered on other options exchanges for adding market maker liquidity in penny-quoted classes, and will continue to incentivize NOM Market Makers to direct liquidity-providing order flow to the Exchange.
The proposed amended rebates to add liquidity in Penny Symbols are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the Exchange would uniformly apply the amended schedule of rebates to any NOM Market Maker that meets the criteria for these rebates. The proposal does not create any new distinction between NOM Market Makers and other market participants, nor between one NOM Market Maker and another; it merely reduces, by a uniform $0.01 per contract, the rebate paid at each of the six tiers. The criteria that a NOM Market Maker must satisfy to qualify for each tier remain unchanged, so a NOM Market Maker that qualifies for a particular tier today will continue to qualify for the same tier under the amended schedule. Furthermore, the amended schedule of rebates is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it remains designed to attract order flow to the Exchange by rewarding NOM Market Makers that contribute liquidity in Penny Symbols. All members and member organizations would benefit from the opportunity to interact with the liquidity that these rebates continue to incentivize.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
Inter-Market Competition
The proposal does not impose an undue burden on inter-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange believes its proposal remains competitive with other options markets and will offer market participants with another choice of where to transact options. The Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily favor competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive, or rebate opportunities available at other venues to be more favorable. In such an environment, the Exchange must continually adjust its fees to remain competitive with other exchanges. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees in response, and because market participants may readily adjust their order routing practices, the Exchange believes that the degree to which fee changes in this market may impose any burden on competition is extremely limited.
Intra-Market Competition
The Exchange's proposed amendments to the rebates paid to NOM Market Makers for adding liquidity in Penny Symbols would not impose an undue burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, because the Exchange would uniformly apply the new schedule of rebates to all NOM Market Makers. Every NOM Market Maker will continue to be eligible to earn the amended rebates on identical terms at each of the six tiers, and each NOM Market Maker's tier assignment will continue to be determined solely by its own level of qualifying activity on the Exchange. The proposal does not modify the qualifying criteria for any tier, nor does it alter the rebates paid to Customers, Professionals, Broker-Dealers, Firms, or Non-NOM Market Makers. Also, the revised schedule of rebates paid to NOM Market Makers for adding liquidity in Penny Symbols is part of the Exchange's overall effort to remain competitive with other options venues and to continue to attract order flow to the Exchange. All members and member organizations would benefit from the opportunity to interact with the liquidity that these rebates continue to incentivize.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
[
16
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is: (i) necessary or appropriate in the public interest; (ii) for the protection of investors; or (iii) otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.

Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:

All submissions should refer to file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-087. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. Manual Transaction Fees of the Fee Schedule To Increase QOO and FOO Order Fees in Non-Penny Interval Classes and To Increase the Floor Broker Enhanced Rebate in Non-Penny Interval Classes

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106664; File No. SR-BOX-2026-20]
October 14, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on September 30, 2026, BOX Exchange LLC (the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act,
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2) thereunder,
[
4
]
which renders the proposal effective upon filing with the Commission. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of the Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) a proposed rule change to amend the Fee Schedule on the BOX Options Market LLC (“BOX”) options facility. The Exchange proposes to increase QOO and FOO Order Fees in Non-Penny Interval classes and to increase the Floor Broker enhanced rebate in Non-Penny Interval classes in Section V. Manual Transaction Fees of the Fee Schedule. While changes to the fee schedule pursuant to this proposal will be effective upon filing, the changes will become operative on October 1, 2026. The text of the proposed rule change is available from the principal office of the Exchange, and also on the Exchange's internet website at
https://rules.boxexchange.com/​rulefilings
.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Section V. Manual Transaction Fees of the Fee Schedule to: (1) increase Market Maker Qualified Open Outcry (“QOO”) and FLEX Open Outcry (“FOO”) Order fees in Non-Penny Interval classes from $0.50 to $1.00; and (2) increase the Floor Broker enhanced rebate in Non-Penny Interval classes from $0.20 to $0.25.
Background of Fees and Rebates for Transactions on the Trading Floor
The Exchange assesses fees (and/or provides rebates) for transactions on the Trading Floor based on account type.
[
5
]
For Public Customers the Exchange does
(
printed page 66177)
not currently assess a per contract fee (or provide a rebate) for QOO and FOO
[
6
]
Orders in all Penny Interval Classes and Non-Penny Interval Classes. The Exchange assesses a $0.10 per contract fee for QOO and FOO orders in Penny Interval Classes and Non-Penny Interval Classes, for the Professional Customer account type. The Exchange assesses a $0.25 per contract fee for QOO and FOO orders in Penny Interval Classes and Non-Penny Interval Classes, for the Broker Dealer account type. The Exchange does not assess a fee (or provide a rebate) for QOO and FOO orders in Penny Interval Classes and Non-Penny Interval Classes, for the Broker Dealer facilitating a Public Customer account type. The Exchange assesses the Market Maker account type a fee of $0.50 per contract for QOO and FOO orders in Penny Interval Classes and Non-Penny Interval Classes.
The Exchange provides Floor Brokers a rebate of $0.10 per contract for all Broker Dealer and Market Maker QOO and FOO Orders presented on the Trading Floor and $0.05 per contract rebate for all Professional Customer QOO and FOO Orders presented on the Trading Floor.
[
7
]
The rebate does not apply to Public Customer executions, executions subject to the Strategy QOO Order Fee Cap and Rebate & Strategy FOO Order Fee Cap and Rebate, or Broker Dealer executions where the Broker Dealer is facilitating a Public Customer. Floor Brokers that submit QOO and FOO Orders receive a $0.20 per contract enhanced rebate for executions that trade with a Floor Market Maker, in lieu of the $0.10 and $0.05 per contract rebates described above. The enhanced rebate does not apply to Public Customer executions, executions subject to the Strategy QOO Order Fee Cap and Rebate & Strategy FOO Order Fee Cap and Rebate, or Broker Dealer executions where the Broker Dealer is facilitating a Public Customer.
Proposal To Increase QOO and FOO Order Fees in Non-Penny Interval Classes for Market Makers
The Exchange proposes to amend the QOO and FOO Order fees in Section V.A. of the Fee Schedule to increase the fee assessed to Market Maker account types in Non-Penny Interval Classes. Currently, the Exchange assesses Market Makers a fee of $0.50 per contract for QOO and FOO Orders in Non-Penny Interval Classes. The Exchange now proposes to assess Market Makers a fee of $1.00 per contract for QOO and FOO Orders in Non-Penny Interval Classes. The purpose of this change is for business and competitive reasons. The Exchange believes that even with the proposed increased fee, the Exchange's transaction fees for Market Maker account types will remain competitive with the fees assessed by other equity options exchanges that offer trading floors for transactions by their market makers in non-penny classes when trading against all other account types.
[
8
]
Proposal To Increase the Enhanced Floor Broker Rebate for QOO and FOO Orders in Non-Penny Interval Classes
Next, the Exchange proposes to amend Section V.C. (QOO and FOO Order Rebate) of the Fee Schedule to increase the per contract enhanced Floor Broker rebate in Non-Penny Interval Classes. Currently, the Exchange provides a Floor Broker enhanced rebate of $0.20 per contract for QOO and FOO Orders for executions that trade with a Floor Market Maker in Penny Interval and Non-Penny Interval Classes. The Exchange now proposes to increase the Floor Broker enhanced rebate to $0.25 per contract for QOO and FOO Orders for executions that trade with a Floor Market Maker in Non-Penny Interval Classes. The Exchange notes that the enhanced rebate does not apply to Public Customer executions, executions subject to Section V.D (Strategy QOO Order Fee Cap and Rebate & Strategy FOO Order Fee Cap and Rebate), or Broker Dealer executions where the Broker Dealer is facilitating a Public Customer. The purpose of this change is for business and competitive reasons.
[
9
]
The Exchange believes this change may encourage additional Floor Broker liquidity in Non-Penny Interval Classes. Additional liquidity in Non-Penny Interval Classes may benefit all market participants because it will attract additional liquidity to BOX by providing more trading opportunities. Further, additional liquidity helps contribute to a robust trading environment on the BOX Trading Floor.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposal is consistent with the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and Section 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
10
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among Participants and other persons using its facilities and does not unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers or dealers.
The Exchange believes the proposal to amend the Market Maker account type to increase the fee to $1.00 per contract for QOO and FOO Order transactions in Non-Penny Interval Classes is reasonable, equitably allocated, and not unfairly discriminatory because, even with the proposed increase, the Exchange believes the proposed fee will not discourage Floor Market Maker order flow. The Exchange notes that even with the proposed increase to the Floor Market Maker fee for transactions in Non-Penny Interval Classes proposed herein, the Exchange's proposed fee of $1.00 per contract for the Market Maker account type in Non-Penny Interval Classes remains competitive with the fee charged by other equity options exchanges to their floor market makers for transactions in non-penny classes.
[
11
]
The Exchange believes that increasing fees for QOO and FOO Order transactions by Market Makers, but not for other market participants, represents an equitable, non-discriminatory allocation of fees because the proposal is based on the type of business transacted by Floor Market Makers on BOX, and Floor Market Makers are not obligated to engage in transactions on the Trading Floor. Rather, Floor Market Makers trade for their own accounts and benefit from having access to interact with orders that are made available in open outcry on the Trading Floor.
The Exchange believes the proposal to increase the Floor Broker enhanced rebate to $0.25 per contract for QOO and FOO Order transactions in Non-Penny Interval Classes is reasonable, equitably allocated and not unfairly discriminatory because the Exchange believes this change may encourage additional Floor Broker liquidity in Non-Penny Interval Classes. The Exchange believes additional liquidity in Non-Penny Interval Classes, to the extent the proposed change accomplishes this goal, may benefit all
(
printed page 66178)
Floor Participants because it will attract additional liquidity to BOX by providing more trading opportunities. Further, additional liquidity helps contribute to a robust trading environment on the BOX Trading Floor.
The Exchange believes the proposed increased Floor Broker enhanced rebate in Non-Penny Interval Classes is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will apply equally to all Floor Brokers who submit orders in Non-Penny Interval Classes on the Trading Floor and have those orders trade with a Floor Market Maker. The Exchange believes the Floor Broker enhanced rebate is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act
[
12
]
because it will continue to encourage market participants to execute orders on the Trading Floor. The Exchange believes that the Floor Broker enhanced rebate could continue to improve liquidity on BOX to the benefit of all market participants. The Exchange notes that providing enhanced rebates to certain market participants is not new or novel. BOX currently provides Floor Broker enhanced rebates in the Fee Schedule.
[
13
]
Additionally, Sapphire provides a Floor Broker Breakup Credit of $0.25 for QFO and cQFO transactions in Non-Penny Classes.
[
14
]
In addition, the proposal is also consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
15
]
because it perfects the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and protects investors and the public interest because it applies equally to all eligible Floor Broker QOO and FOO Orders and access to the Exchange is offered on terms that are not unfairly discriminatory.
The Exchange believes it is equitable to apply the proposed enhanced rebate only to Floor Brokers and not Floor Market Makers. Floor Market Makers represent their own interest on the Trading Floor and, therefore, the Exchange believes these market participants may not need a similar incentive. Additionally, Floor Market Makers may choose to conduct their business on a trading floor or in an electronic market, unlike Floor Brokers, who have a business model that is naturally tied to the physical trading space. The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is equitable because the proposed rebate is based on the amount and type of business transacted on BOX, and Floor Brokers may elect to earn the proposed enhanced rebate if they choose. The Exchange also believes that providing the proposed rebate to Floor Brokers is equitable because it is intended to support Floor Brokers' role in facilitating the execution of open outcry orders, a function which benefits all market participants on the Trading Floor.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
Intermarket Competition
The proposal does not impose an undue burden on intermarket competition. The Exchange believes its proposal remains competitive with other options exchanges that charge similar fees and provide rebates and this proposal will offer market participants with another choice of where to transact options.
[
16
]
The Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily favor competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive, or rebate opportunities available at other venues to be more favorable. In such an environment, the Exchange must continually adjust its fees and rebates to remain competitive with other exchanges. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees or rebates in response, and because market participants may readily adjust their order routing practices, the Exchange believes that the degree to which fee and rebate changes in this market may impose any burden on competition is extremely limited. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change reflects this competitive environment because it modifies the Exchange's fees and rebates in a manner designed to continue to incentivize participants on the Trading Floor to direct trading interest to BOX, to provide liquidity and to attract additional order flow. For the reasons described above, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change reflects this competitive environment.
Intra-Market Competition
The proposal does not impose an undue burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange believes that the proposed change would encourage the submission of additional liquidity to a public exchange, thereby promoting market depth, price discovery and transparency and enhancing order execution opportunities for all market participants. As a result, the Exchange believes that the proposed change furthers the Commission's goal in adopting Regulation NMS of fostering integrated competition among orders. The proposed changes are designed to attract additional order flow to the Trading Floor.
The Exchange believes that the proposed fee assessed to Floor Market Maker orders in Non-Penny Interval Classes and the proposed enhanced Floor Broker rebate in Non-Penny Interval Classes would encourage Floor Broker open outcry order flow and would not disincentivize Floor Market Maker activity on the Trading Floor. The Exchange does not believe that Floor Market Makers will be discouraged from transacting on the Trading Floor, as Floor Market Makers trade for their own accounts and benefit from having access to interact with orders that are made available in open outcry on the Trading Floor. The Exchange also believes that Floor Market Maker fees relative to other market participants do not impose an undue burden on competition because Floor Market Makers are not obligated to engage in transactions on the Trading Floor. To the extent that there is an additional competitive burden on Floor Market Makers, the Exchange believes that any such burden would be appropriate because Floor Brokers serve an important function in facilitating the execution of orders and price discovery for all market participants. Further, to the extent this proposal is successful, it will increase trading opportunities for Floor Market Makers because Floor Market Makers trade for their own accounts and benefit from having the opportunity to interact with orders that are made available in open outcry on the Trading Floor. Greater liquidity benefits all market participants on BOX and increased order flow would increase opportunities for execution of other trading interest. The proposed modifications would apply and be available to all similarly-situated market participants that execute open outcry orders on the Trading Floor, and, accordingly, the proposed changes would not impose a disparate burden on competition among market participants on BOX.
(
printed page 66179)
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Exchange Act
[
17
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2) thereunder,
[
18
]
because it establishes or changes a due, or fee.
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend the rule change if it appears to the Commission that the action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or would otherwise further the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-BOX-2026-20 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-BOX-2026-20. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-BOX-2026-20 and should be submitted on or before November 9, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.

]

Assistant Secretary.

I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to make certain amendments to its warrant performance incentive program. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://equities.24exchange.com/​regulation
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange adopted a warrant performance incentive program (“Program”) to allow Members of the Exchange who participate in the Program (“Participants”)
[
3
]
to earn the right to purchase Non-Voting Common Units
[
4
]
of 24X US Holdings LLC (“24X US Holdco”), the Exchange's parent company.
[
5
]
As described in the Warrant Program Release, each Member of the Exchange may become a Participant in the Program by prepaying $500,000 in Exchange fees (“Prepayment Fee”) and satisfying the Program eligibility requirements.
[
6
]
Upon joining the Program, each Participant will receive a warrant that vests based on the Participant's achievement of certain minimum trading volumes (“Target Volume”)
[
7
]
on the Exchange during each designated pre-determined period in which the Program is in effect (“Measurement Period”)
[
8
]
and the Exchange's achievement of a minimum market share during such Measurement Periods (“24X Minimum Overall Market Share”).
[
9
]
When the warrants vest, Participants will have the right to exercise the warrants to purchase a certain number of 24X US Holdco Non-Voting Common Units.
The Exchange has determined to revise the Program to make additional Non-Voting Common Units available to be purchased by Participants starting in the first Measurement Period of 2027 (“Additional Equity”), under different terms than those applicable to the Non-Voting Common Units currently available to be purchased through the Program (“Original Equity”). Specifically, the right to purchase Additional Equity would extend through two additional Measurement Periods in 2028, would be subject to a reduced Prepayment Fee, and would be based on maker volume only instead of total trading volume.
(
printed page 66183)
The Exchange also proposes to make two additional changes to the terms of the Program that would apply to the right to purchase both the Original Equity and the Additional Equity. Specifically, as described below, the Exchange proposes to eliminate the 24X Minimum Overall Market Share threshold requirement and exclude certain dates from the calculation of Target Volume in each Measurement Period. All other aspects of the Program would remain the same as described in the Warrant Program Releases.
The Exchange proposes to implement the rule change on October 1, 2026. None of the proposed changes would be applied retroactively.

As described below, the Exchange proposes that depending on which Prepayment Fee they elect to pay, Participants of the Program may become eligible to earn either (i) the right to purchase both Original Equity and Additional Equity or (ii) the right to purchase Additional Equity only.
ii. Prepayment Fee
The Exchange proposes that current Participants of the Program who have already paid the $500,000 Prepayment Fee will be automatically eligible to earn the right to purchase Additional Equity for any Measurement Period in which the Program thresholds are met, as long as those Participants continue to meet the other Program eligibility requirements. The Exchange also proposes that any Participant who joins the Program after the proposed rule change goes into effect can either (i) prepay $500,000 in Exchange fees to become eligible to earn the right to purchase both Original Equity and Additional Equity, or (ii) prepay a reduced amount of $250,000 in Exchange fees to become eligible to earn the right to purchase Additional Equity only. The Prepayment Fee must be tendered by the first day of each quarter of the Program Period to participate in the Program as of such quarter until April 1, 2028.
The following are examples of the timing of participation in the Program:
If Participant A joined the Program by tendering the $500,000 Prepayment Fee and executing the required documentation on October 14, 2025 (the date trading commenced on the Exchange), then Participant A's trading starting on October 14, 2025 would be counted toward the Target Volume for Year 1 and thereafter until the end of the Program Period. Participant A would be eligible to earn the right to purchase both Original Equity and Additional Equity for the entire Program Period.
If Participant B joined the Program by tendering the $500,000 Prepayment Fee and executing the required documentation on October 22, 2026, then Participant B's trading starting on January 1, 2027 would be counted toward the Target Volume for the first quarter of Year 3 (
i.e.,
the first Measurement Period for Year 3) and thereafter until the end of the Program Period. Participant B would be eligible to earn the right to purchase both Original Equity and Additional Equity starting with the Measurement Period that begins on January 1, 2027 throughout the end of the Program Period.
If Participant C joined the Program by tendering the $250,000 Prepayment Fee and executing the required documentation on October 22, 2026, then Participant C's trading starting on January 1, 2027 would be counted toward the Target Volume for the first quarter of Year 3 (
i.e.,
the first Measurement Period for Year 3) and thereafter until the end of the Program Period. Participant C would be eligible to earn the right to purchase Additional Equity only starting with the Measurement Period that begins on January 1, 2027 throughout the end of the Program Period.
If Participant D joined the Program by tendering the $500,000 Prepayment Fee and executing the required documentation on October 1, 2027, then Participant D's trading starting on October 1, 2027 would be counted toward the Target Volume for the fourth quarter of Year 3 (
i.e.,
the last Measurement Period in Year 3) and the first quarter of Year 4 (
i.e.,
the only Measurement Period in Year 4). Participant D would be eligible to earn both the right to purchase Original Equity for the last Measurement Period in Year 3 and the right to purchase Additional Equity for the last Measurement Period in Year 3 and the only two Measurement Periods in Year 4. No Member may become a Participant that is eligible to earn Original Equity after October 1, 2027.
If Participant E joined the Program by tendering the $250,000 Prepayment Fee and executing the required documentation on April 1, 2028, then Participant E's trading starting on April 1, 2028 would be counted toward the Target Volume for the second quarter of Year 4 (
i.e.,
the second Measurement Period in Year 4). Participant E would be eligible to earn the right to purchase Additional Equity for the second Measurement Period in Year 4. No Member may become a Participant after April 1, 2028.
All other terms regarding the Prepayment Fee would remain unchanged as described in the Warrant Program Releases.
iii. Target Volume Calculation
As described in the Warrant Program Release, the Target Volume that Participants must meet in order for their warrants to vest is 5% of the average daily trading volume on the Exchange, where the daily trading volume is calculated based on total aggregated average daily volume traded over each Measurement Period.
[
12
]
The Exchange proposes that with respect to Additional Equity only, Target Volume for each
(
printed page 66185)
Measurement Period will be calculated based solely on Participants' maker volume (
i.e.,
trading volume which adds liquidity to the Exchange). Target Volume will continue to be calculated based on total trading volume with respect to Original Equity.
Pursuant to the Program requirements, the Non-Voting Common Units subject to the Program would be allocated among Participants who have met or outperformed the Target Volume during each Measurement Period on a pro rata basis based on volume contributions to the 24X market. As described in the Warrant Program Release, the volumes for each Participant are calculated for each of the Measurement Periods,
[
13
]
and the Non-Voting Common Units indicated are allocated among Participants after the end of each Measurement Period. With respect to Additional Equity only, the Exchange proposes to add two Measurement Periods during the first and second quarters of Year 4. Therefore, the Non-Voting Common Units that would be available to be purchased for the first Measurement Period of Year 4 in accordance with the Program will be allocated among Participants that meet the Target Volume on or before April 5, 2028 and after March 31, 2028, based on trading during the first Measurement Period of Year 4, which is the quarterly period from January 1, 2028 through March 31, 2028. The Non-Voting Common Units that would be available to be purchased for the second Measurement Period of Year 4 in accordance with the Program will be allocated among Participants that meet the Target Volume on or before July 5, 2028 and after June 30, 2028, based on trading during the second Measurement Period of Year 4, which is the quarterly period from April 1, 2028 through June 30, 2028. All other terms regarding Target Volume would remain unchanged as described in the Warrant Program Releases.
b. Proposed Changes With Respect to Both Original Equity and Additional Equity
i. Elimination of 24X Minimum Overall Market Share Threshold
As described in the Warrant Program Releases, the 24X Minimum Overall Market Share is a designated target percentage of the CADV for all NMS Stocks eligible for trading on 24X for each relevant Measurement Period.
[
14
]
The CADV is calculated based on the volume reported by all exchanges and trade reporting facilities to a consolidated transaction reporting plan for the relevant Measurement Period.
In order to incentivize participation in the Program and bring greater volume and liquidity to the Exchange, the Exchange proposes to eliminate the 24X Minimum Overall Market Share requirement with respect to Original Equity, and to not implement a 24X Minimum Overall Market Share requirement with respect to Additional Equity. Elimination of the requirement would make Program outcomes more predictable for Participants because Exchange market share depends on the trading activity of all Members and on changes in overall U.S. equity market volume, rather than the individual actions of each Participant. By allowing Participants to determine whether their warrants will vest solely by choosing to meet the Target Volume and not having to rely on other factors outside their control, the proposed revised Program would both attract more new Participants and encourage existing Participants to increase the amount of liquidity they contribute to the Exchange. The Exchange also notes that another national securities exchange offers a warrant program that does not include an exchange market share threshold as a warrant vesting condition.
[

]
