2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act
[
16
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act
[
17
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act
[
18
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Exchange Act,
[
19
]
which requires that Exchange rules provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its members and other persons using its facilities.
The Exchange believes that the proposed changes to the Program are consistent with the Act. Making the Additional Equity available for purchase through the Program at a reduced Prepayment Fee and based on maker volume only would both encourage additional Participant enrollment in the Program, and encourage Participants to provide additional volume and liquidity to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that an increase in volume and liquidity would benefit all market participants by providing more trading opportunities and tighter spreads, even to those market participants that do not participate in the Program, thereby perfecting the mechanism for a free and open market and national market system.
Moreover, the elimination of the 24X Minimum Overall Market Share requirement and exclusion of certain dates from the calculation of Target Volume with respect to both Original Equity and Additional Equity would make it more likely that Participants' warrants would vest in any given Measurement Period. As described above, elimination of the 24X Minimum Overall Market Share requirement would allow Participants to have more control over whether their warrants vest in any given Measurement Period,
[
20
]
and exclusion of certain dates from the calculation of Target Volume would remove a potential diluting effect that otherwise would hamper Participants' ability to achieve Target Volume through ordinary trading activity. These incentives would promote the long-term interests of the Exchange by attracting new Participants and encouraging existing Participants to contribute to the growth and success of the Exchange via actively providing liquidity on the 24X market, and to provide additional investment and funding which could be used for the regulation and operation of the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the additional funds provided as a result of these changes would enable the Exchange to have greater capacity to carry out the purposes of the Act and to comply with the provisions of the Act, the rules and regulations thereunder, and the rules of the Exchange, which, in turn, would protect investors and the public interest.
The Exchange believes that the proposed changes are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because all Participants may earn the right to purchase both Original Equity and Additional Equity on the same terms and conditions. The additional Measurement Period, Prepayment Fee schedule, and Target Volume modification with respect to Additional Equity are objective and the same for all Participants. Likewise, the elimination of the 24X Minimum Overall Market Share requirement and exclusion of certain dates from the calculation of Target Volume with respect to both Additional Equity and Original Equity are based on objective standards and would have the same effect for all Participants.
A Participant's total equity ownership of 24X US Holdco Units, including any purchased through the exercise of vested warrants via the Program, shall be subject to the ownership limitations of the 24X US Holdco LLC Agreement.
[
21
]
Accordingly, a Participant will not be able to exercise warrants for Non-Voting Common Units to the extent that such exercise would violate such ownership limitations.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Exchange Act. The Exchange believes that the Program as amended by this proposed rule change would increase both intermarket and intramarket competition by incentivizing Participants to add liquidity to the Exchange, which will enhance the quality of quoting and increase the volume of securities traded on the Exchange. To the extent that there is an additional competitive burden on non-Participants, the Exchange believes that such burden is appropriate because the Program should incentivize Participants to add liquidity to the Exchange and thus enhance the volume of securities traded on the Exchange. To the extent that this purpose is achieved, the Exchange believes that all of the Exchange's market participants would benefit from the improved market liquidity.
Given the robust competition for volume among equities markets, implementing a program to attract liquidity addition like the one proposed in this filing is consistent with the abovementioned goals of the Exchange Act. This is especially true for the smaller exchange markets, such as 24X, which are competing for volume with much larger exchanges that dominate the equities trading industry. As a new exchange, 24X will likely continue to have a nominal percentage of the average daily trading volume in equities in the near term, so it is unlikely that the Program could cause any competitive harm to the equities market or to market participants. Rather, the Program is a modest attempt to attract order volume away from larger competitors by adopting an innovative pricing strategy. The Exchange notes that if the Program results in a modest percentage increase in the average daily trading volume on 24X, while such percentage would represent a large volume increase for 24X, it would represent a minimal reduction in volume of its larger competitors in the industry. The Exchange believes that the Program will help further competition, because market participants will have yet another option in determining where to post liquidity if they factor the benefits of 24X equity participation into the determination.

Department of Agriculture
Forest Service
AGENCY:
Forest Service, USDA.
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
The Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit proposes to establish several recreation fee sites. Proposed recreation fees collected at the proposed recreation fee sites would be used for operation, maintenance, and improvement of the sites. An analysis of nearby recreation fee sites with similar amenities shows that the proposed recreation fees are reasonable and typical of similar recreation fee sites in the area.
DATES:
If approved, the proposed recreation fee sites and proposed recreation fees would be established no earlier than six months following the publication of this notice in the
Federal Register
.
ADDRESSES:
Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Attention: Recreation Fees, 35 College Drive, South Lake Tahoe, CA 96150.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Lisa Herron, Public Affairs Specialist, (530) 721-3898,
SM.FS.R5.LTBMU.FeeProposal@usda.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The Federal Lands Recreation Enhancement Act (
16 U.S.C. 6803(b)
) requires the Forest Service to publish in the
Federal Register
a six-month advance notice before establishment of proposed recreation fee sites. In accordance with Forest Service Handbook 2309.13, Chapter 30, the Forest Service will publish the proposed recreation fee sites, and proposed recreation fees in local newspapers and other local publications for public comment. At least 80 percent of the proposed recreation fees collected at the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit would remain available for expenditure at the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit to enhance the visitor experience at the proposed recreation fee sites
A proposed expanded amenity recreation fee of $20 per night would be charged for Luther Pass Overflow Campground and Watson Lake Campground.
A proposed standard amenity recreation fee of $10 per day per vehicle would be charged at 64 Acres Riverside Picnic Site, Echo Trailhead, and Kiva Picnic Area (Tallac Historic Area) developed recreation sites. Additionally, a proposed standard amenity recreation fee of $10 per day per vehicle for the first year of implementation, and $15 per day per vehicle, after five years of implementation, would be charged for Big Meadow Trailhead, Kiva Beach, and Taylor Creek Visitor Center. The America the Beautiful—the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Pass would be honored at these standard amenity recreation fee sites.
Fee revenue would be used to enhance recreation opportunities, improve customer service, and address maintenance needs.
Once public involvement is complete, the proposed recreation fee sites will be reviewed by a Resource Advisory Committee prior to a final decision and implementation. Reservations for campgrounds and cabins could be made online at
www.recreation.gov
or by calling (877) 444-6777. Reservations would cost $8.00 per reservation. A Reservation fee of $8.00 per reservation will be added to the cost of the reservation. The $8.00 reservation fee is a transaction fee charged by the
recreation.gov
reservation platform and is not a Forest Service recreation fee under the Federal Lands Recreation Enhancement Act. This transaction fee is retained by the service provider to support the cost of the reservation system.
Gordon Blum,
Associate Deputy Chief, Recreation and Heritage.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Table of Contents
I. Introduction
II. Background
III. Commission Analysis
IV. Ordering Paragraphs
I. Introduction
On October 13, 2026, the Postal Service filed a motion for extension of time to submit its response to Chairman's Information Request No. 1 (CHIR No.1), seeking to extend the current deadline of October 14, 2026, to October 21, 2026.
[
1
]
For the reasons discussed below, the Commission grants the Motion. In addition, the Commission extends the deadline for comments from October 16, 2026, to October 26, 2026.
II. Background
On September 16, 2026, the Postal Service filed a request to remove
Mail Classification Schedule
(MCS) section 2615.2 Competitive International Registered Mail from the Competitive product list and make accompanying classification changes in MCS sections 2340.5 and 2600.2, effective January 1, 2027.
[
2
]
In addition, the Postal Service also requests to transfer the Inbound PRIME Registered Service Agreement 1 and the PRIME-USPS Registered Agreement from the Competitive product list to the Market Dominant product list, and add these two agreements to MCS section 1602.3.5 Inbound Market Dominant Multi-Service Agreements with Foreign Postal Operators 1, effective January 1, 2027. Request at 1-2, 4.
On September 17, 2026, the Commission established the instant docket, appointed a Public Representative, and set October 16, 2026 as the deadline for comments.
[
3
]
On October 7, 2026, CHIR No. 1 was issued.
[
4
]
The deadline for responding to CHIR No. 1 is October 14, 2026. CHIR No. 1 at 1.
On October 13, 2026, the Postal Service filed the Motion. The Postal Service states that it is preparing its response to CHIR No. 1 but needs additional time to finalize its response. Motion at 1. The Postal Service requests an extension of 7 days until October 21, 2026 to submit its response to CHIR No. 1.
Id.
The Postal Service notes that it would not object if any interested party requests a brief extension of the comment deadline or seeks to file supplement comments.
Id.,
n.2.
III. Commission Analysis
The proposed effective date for the proposed classification changes is January 1, 2027. Request at 3, 4. Therefore, extending the deadline for the Postal Service to respond to CHIR No. 1 by 7 calendar days would not have any adverse impact on the overall procedural schedule of this docket, nor would it have any adverse impact on other participants. Accordingly, the Commission grants the Motion and extends the deadline for responding to CHIR No. 1 to October 21, 2026.
39 CFR 3010.162(c)
.
In addition, the Commission extends the deadline set in Order No. 9732 for comments from October 16, 2026 to October 26, 2026, so that interested participants will have sufficient time to review the Postal Service's response to CHIR No. 1 and consider it in preparing their comments.
IV. Ordering Paragraphs
It is ordered:
1. The United States Postal Service Motion for Extension of Time to File Response to Chairman's Information Request No. 1, filed October 13, 2026, is granted.
2. The response to Chairman's Information Request No. 1 is due October 21, 2026.
3. Comments are due October 26, 2026.
4. This Order, or an abstract thereof, shall be published in the
Federal Register
.
By the Commission.
Parvaneh Higareda,
Senior Paralegal Specialist.

Title:
Great American Digital Corridors (GADC) Program.
Background:
The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), in partnership with the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Research and Technology, administers the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Great American Digital Corridors (GADC) Program Cooperative Agreement. The GADC Program was authorized under Section 11101(c)(1)(D) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) (
Pub. L. 117-58
) to carry out the Intelligent Transportation Systems Program pursuant to Title 23, United States Code (U.S.C.) §§ 512-518.
The purpose of the GADC Program is to support States and eligible entities in advancing the deployment of digital infrastructure along the Federal-aid highway system, including the Interstate System. The program's goals include modernizing the digital infrastructure of the Federal-aid highway system, including the Interstate System, to improve safety and efficiency, reduce congestion, and optimize freight movement. Digital infrastructure supports the modernization of transportation systems by enabling the exchange of precise, accurate, and reliable digital feeds of work zones, lane closures, and other dynamic, real-time operational conditions. By using digital infrastructure to bridge the gap between physical infrastructure and digital intelligence, infrastructure owner-operators can improve safety, efficiency, security, and mobility for transportation workers and all road users.
The program provides competitive cost-reimbursable cooperative agreements to eligible entities, including States, local and Tribal governments, transit agencies, public toll authorities, Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), other political subdivisions of a State or local government, private entities, nonprofit organizations, and
(
printed page 66193)
academic institutions may apply as an eligible entity and lead administration of the project, provided they apply as part of consortium with one or more other eligible entities, and consortiums of eligible entities. The Federal share for GADC projects is 100 percent, requiring no non-Federal match. The FHWA announced the availability of up to $20 million for fiscal year 2026 funding to support these digital infrastructure improvements.
Respondents:
The NOFO announcing up to $20 million of Fiscal Year (FY) 2026, funding for GADC cooperative agreement will be available for eligible respondents entities, including States, local and Tribal governments, transit agencies, public toll authorities, Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), other political subdivisions of a State or local government, private entities, nonprofit organizations, and academic institutions may apply as an eligible entity and lead administration of the project, provided they apply as part of consortium with one or more other eligible entities, and consortiums of eligible entities. FHWA is expecting approximately 20 applicants to apply for the GADC cooperative agreement.
Frequency:
NOFOs and cooperative agreement solicitations may be published annually by FHWA but, are subject to the availability of funds in appropriations or, any legislation signed into law authorizing funds.
Estimated Average Burden per Response:
10 hours per respondent per applicant.
Estimated Total Annual Burden Hours:
It is expected that the respondents will complete approximately 20 applications for the program, for an estimated total of 200 annual burden hours (10hrs × 20 = 200hrs).
Public Comments Invited:
You are asked to comment on any aspect of this information collection, including: (1) Whether the proposed collection is necessary for the FHWA's performance; (2) the accuracy of the estimated burdens; (3) ways for the FHWA to enhance the quality, usefulness, and clarity of the collected information; and (4) ways that the burden could be minimized, including the use of electronic technology, without reducing the quality of the collected information. The agency will summarize and/or include your comments in the request for OMB's clearance of this information collection.
